FFmpeg: source, build instructions and replacement

This distribution contains the separate ffmpeg.dll supplied with Electron 45.0.0 Windows x64. The vendored Chromium FFmpeg source is LGPL v2.1 or later with separately licensed components. Full notices are in LICENSES.chromium.html.

Electron official release archive SHA-256: ae53887a23bb640369c93dbd38c408a2af5c0deb86f2fa76c6c244cb444b7f47
Installed ffmpeg.dll SHA-256: cdf2b70f0f0a97c9840af1466dd86a90e564c98f6892d783635cf9c3b303d613
FFmpeg source revision: 9db86ce5b5b454dfc96c435f9f0723012980c37f, selected by Chromium 156.0.8078.48.
The official Electron release job links the DLL built with release.gn (Chrome branding, component FFmpeg, x64). The Chromium generated Chrome/win/x64 configuration sets CONFIG_GPL=0, CONFIG_NONFREE=0, CONFIG_VERSION3=0 and CONFIG_LIBOPUS=1. The standalone Electron ffmpeg asset uses different codec flags.

The corresponding source package includes the pinned FFmpeg and Opus sources, Electron source and patch, Chromium DEPS, license notices and build instructions. See SOURCE-BUILD.txt and the source-files.json manifest. Download the source package and checksums alongside the Windows executables:
https://github.com/qtaro-dev/Server-Control-Studio/releases/tag/v0.1.0

Installer: close the application and replace ffmpeg.dll next to Server Control Studio.exe with an ABI-compatible build.
Portable: extract the .7z app payload from the wrapper using an NSIS-capable archive utility. Extract that payload to a writable folder, replace ffmpeg.dll beside Server Control Studio.exe and run that executable from the folder. The original Portable launcher always uses its own embedded DLL.

Official release job: https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/39539521491/job/119024612478
FFmpeg distribution guidance: https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html
